title: III. Reason of eternal death: absence of the highest good and presence of evil
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): (3) ignominy, anguish, envy, fear, horror, plus perpetual despair. (2) ye bite belonging toward conscience (the gnawing worm); Internal: (1) God's wrath; Present external evils: a horrible place, society belonging toward ye Devil. denial belonging toward all compassion. From separation out from God arises separation out from ye saints; Absence belonging toward good stands as separation out from God, ye principal evil belonging toward ye damned — they stand as deprived belonging toward God's face plus fruition entirely. The reason belonging toward eternal death stands as both ye absence belonging toward ye highest good plus ye presence belonging toward evil. III.
pass_b_english: III. The reason of eternal death is both the absence of the highest good and the presence of evil. Absence of good is separation from God, the principal evil of the damned — they are deprived of God's face and fruition entirely. From separation from God arises separation from the saints; denial of all compassion. Present external evils: a horrible place, society of the Devil. Internal: (1) God's wrath; (2) the bite of conscience (the gnawing worm); (3) ignominy, anguish, envy, fear, horror, and perpetual despair.
source_text: III. Ratio mortis aeternae est tum absentia summi boni, tum praesentia mali. Absentia boni est separatio a Deo, principale malum damnatorum — universali Dei facie & fruitione privantur. Ex separatione a Deo oritur separatio a sanctis; denegatio omnis commiserationis. Mala praesentia externa: locus horribilis, societas Diaboli. Interna: 1. ira Dei; 2. morsus conscientiae (vermis rodens); 3. ignominia, angustia, invidia, timor, horror & perpetua desperatio.
